title: Migration Strategy Decision Tree: Big-Bang vs Phased
description: Decision tree for choosing between big-bang (all modules at once) and phased (incremental module rollout) migration strategies for life sciences CRM. Factors include organizational complexity, risk tolerance, module interdependencies, and operational constraints.

nodes.question: How many countries will go live on the target platform?
nodes.guidance: Country count is the primary driver of migration complexity. Each country adds regulatory configuration, localization, user training, and data migration scope.

nodes.question: How many modules are in scope for migration?
nodes.guidance: Count distinct functional modules: Visit Management, Sample Management, Consent Management, Content Management, Field Email, Events Management, Territory Alignment, Activity Plans, Medical Information, etc.

nodes.question: How many modules are in scope for migration?
nodes.guidance: With multiple countries, module count amplifies complexity — each module needs per-country configuration and testing.

nodes.question: How many end users will be migrated?
nodes.guidance: User count affects training logistics, data migration volume, and rollback complexity.

nodes.question: What is the organization's tolerance for a parallel-run period?
nodes.guidance: A parallel-run period means running both source and target platforms simultaneously. This reduces risk but increases cost and user burden. Consider whether the source platform contract timeline forces a hard cutover date.

options.label: No parallel run — hard cutover date required
Willing to run parallel for 2-4 weeks

requirements: Phase 1: Core modules first — Visit Management + Territory Alignment + Activity Plans (these are tightly coupled and should migrate together)
Phase 2: Compliance modules — Sample Management + Consent Management (these have regulatory dependencies that benefit from a stable core)
Phase 3: Communication modules — Field Email + Content Management (depend on consent configuration from Phase 2)
Phase 4: Advanced modules — Events Management, Medical Information, Analytics
Each phase should include: data migration dry run, user acceptance testing, training, and a go/no-go gate
Plan 4-8 weeks per phase depending on module complexity
Maintain data synchronization between source and target during transition
Define clear criteria for decommissioning the source platform
nodes.recommendation: Phased migration is recommended. The combination of country count, module count, or user count creates too much simultaneous change risk for a big-bang approach. Phased migration allows learning from early phases, limits blast radius of issues, and gives users time to adapt.

requirements: Big-bang migration is viable for this scope
Plan a single cutover weekend with pre-migrated data and pre-tested configuration
Conduct at least 2 full data migration dry runs before the cutover
Prepare a documented rollback plan with a decision deadline (e.g., 4 hours post-cutover)
Train all users before cutover — do not rely on post-go-live training
Staff a war room for the first 2 weeks post-go-live with dedicated support
Pre-configure all reports and dashboards — users expect day-one parity
nodes.recommendation: Big-bang migration is feasible given the limited scope. The key risk is that any misconfiguration affects all users simultaneously. Mitigate with thorough dry runs and a clear rollback plan.

requirements: Big-bang migration under a hard cutover deadline requires additional safeguards
Start data migration dry runs at least 8 weeks before cutover
Run a minimum of 3 full dry runs, fixing issues between each
Establish a go/no-go decision gate 48 hours before cutover with defined criteria
Build a rollback plan that can execute within 4 hours — test the rollback plan itself
Pre-stage all user training and have floor-walker support for the first week
Over-staff the support desk for 2 weeks post-cutover
Validate every integration point (downstream systems, data warehouses, third-party tools) in a staging environment that mirrors production
nodes.recommendation: Big-bang migration is necessary given the hard cutover constraint, but carry elevated risk. The lack of parallel-run means the rollback plan is the primary safety net — invest heavily in testing it.

requirements: Hybrid approach: migrate all modules in a single cutover but run parallel systems for a transition period
During parallel-run: source platform is read-only (historical reference), target platform is the system of record
Do NOT allow data entry in both systems simultaneously — this creates reconciliation nightmares
Use the parallel period for: issue discovery, user support escalation, data validation, and report comparison
Set a firm end-date for parallel-run — open-ended parallel periods erode adoption
Plan data migration in a single batch, not incrementally, to avoid synchronization complexity
nodes.recommendation: The hybrid approach balances risk and timeline. Migrating everything at once simplifies data integrity, while the parallel-run period provides a safety net. The critical discipline is keeping the source platform read-only during parallel-run.
